open_points.subject: open_store
open_points.text: - open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on data_directory itself, opened as a directory without following links and held for the life of the process, so the lock creates no file; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link; create its tables with create_store_schema, which leaves existing tables as they are; then remove the temporary files an interrupted publish left in the content-addressed area and every file of that area whose digest no StoredValue names — a trial case's file fixture is itself a StoredValue of file carriage (M21), so no other record names a value file —, which is a digest for which list_stored_value_rows_by_value_digest answers no row, and create the content-addressed area when absent; last, call remove_spool_temporaries for data_directory, which creates the spool area when absent and removes the temporaries of an interrupted spool publish, re-raising its SpoolInternalError as StoreInternalError.
open_points.other_text: - open_store: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns StoreOpened with data_directory and temporary_files_removed, the count of temporary files removed from the content-addressed area plus the count remove_spool_temporaries returns, unnamed value files not counted; no record, named value file or spool is removed by this call; the spools of ended runs are removed later in the start sequence, by run recovery (A18 rule 4).
open_points.question: Must open_store remove spool temporary files through remove_spool_temporaries, or must no spool be removed by this call?

open_points.subject: record_change lifecycle status validation
open_points.text: - record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. It checks no status of the record a lifecycle change updates and sets that change's fields whatever status the record has: the status a change may start from is the caller's rule, and one request ends before the next begins (A18), so no other request can have changed it meanwhile. A record of a kind the security-boundary note names never updated is only ever written once; a lifecycle change updates the fields its variant sets on the one record the change names, in place, and no other field of a written record ever changes.
open_points.other_text: - record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] ProposeBindingChange writes an OperationBinding with status proposed; AcceptBindingChange sets a proposed binding to accepted with accepted_at; ComposeFlowVersionChange writes the FlowVersion and its StoredValues, plus the Flow with created_flow_purpose as purpose when that is given; ActivateFlowVersionChange writes one FlowActivation; StartRunChange writes a Run with status running, its pinned implementations, inputs and StoredValues and no waiting points.
open_points.question: Must AcceptBindingChange apply whatever the binding's current status is, or only when the binding is proposed?

A record of a kind the security-boundary note names never updated is only ever written once; a lifecycle change updates the fields its variant sets on the one record the change names, in place, and no other field of a written record ever changes.
open_points.other_text: - record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] RequestApprovalChange writes an EffectApproval with status requested; DecideApprovalChange sets a requested approval to approved or refused per the = models.OwnerDecision value with decided_at and, for a refusal, writes its refusal_execution as the element's NodeExecution; RecordAttemptInFlightChange writes an EffectAttempt with status in_flight and the inputs the change carries; RecordAttemptOutcomeChange sets the in_flight attempt's status and concluded_at, writes its concluding NodeExecution, StoredValues and SpooledFiles and sets the approval named by used_approval_id to used.
open_points.question: Must DecideApprovalChange and RecordAttemptOutcomeChange apply whatever the current status is, or only to a requested approval and an in_flight attempt respectively?

A record of a kind the security-boundary note names never updated is only ever written once; a lifecycle change updates the fields its variant sets on the one record the change names, in place, and no other field of a written record ever changes.
open_points.other_text: - record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] RecordReadOutcomeChange writes the concluding NodeExecution with its StoredValues and SpooledFiles and no attempt; RecordOperationFailureChange writes one NodeExecution and no attempt; ResolveAttemptChange sets an unknown attempt's status to the AttemptStatus member named like its AttemptResolution (applied or not_applied) and its resolved_by; a resolution records no time of its own; GrantChange writes a StandingGrant with status active; RevokeChange sets an active grant to revoked with revoked_at; RecoverInFlightChange sets one in_flight attempt to unknown with concluded_at, writes its NodeExecution when given and sets used_approval_id's approval to used when given.
open_points.question: Must ResolveAttemptChange, RevokeChange and RecoverInFlightChange apply whatever the current status is, or only to unknown, active and in_flight records respectively?
